stages.title: Monopoly power and price discrimination
stages.sub: Why monopolies can split markets to charge different prices, and who gains or loses from monopoly power.

steps.q: A firm with monopoly power charges high prices and keeps output low compared with a competitive market. What does this let it earn, period after period?
steps.hint: Without rivals able to enter and undercut it, what happens to its profit over time?

steps.q: That profit could fund research into better products, but the same monopoly also restricts output and charges more than a competitive market would. Is this good or bad for buyers?
steps.right: Mixed: pricier now, better products later
steps.wrong: Fully bad, with no upside ever
steps.hint: Weigh the higher price and lower output against any future gains from research spending.

steps.q: A large, stable monopoly firm rarely goes bust and may keep its workforce for years, but because it produces less output than a competitive market would, does it need as many workers as a competitive industry making the same good?
steps.right: No, it needs fewer workers overall
steps.hint: Lower output from the whole industry means less need for labour across it, even if existing jobs feel secure.
